ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Days on the colony calendar come round once a year. Keep them, and in three years they become traditions everyone looks forward to; a keeper of days on the council makes each one a little more of an occasion.
A day of remembrance is sad and good at once. Keep it each year, and keep the graves tidy and close, so there's somewhere for it to go.
Every year a colonist stays is marked, and their friends are glad of it too. Nothing to do but keep them here.
Friends who look after someone getting over an illness are remembered for it. Rest in bed gets them well a third sooner; the advisor warns when a convalescent is back at work.
A story in stages that ended well. The World page shows the stories still unfolding; the answer the council gives at each stage decides how the next one goes.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A story that went badly. It fades in a few days; a friend's company or a good evening helps it pass. Next time, the World page shows what's still unfolding, and the colony's answers decide the next stage.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: An heirloom is a comfort as long as it's carried, more so to the heir: keep it out of the stockpile and on them. Watching a child grow up is its own reward.

ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.fix: A feeling the colony started the game with. It fades over a month or more; shared work, shared meals and a common enemy bring feuding families together sooner.
ColonyCouncil.MoodHintDef.keep: Something the colony started the game with. It lasts for a season or more, and the bonds it began can grow into lasting friendships on the Bonds page.

A seasonal custom kept, or a day marked properly. Choose the same answer two years running and it becomes a tradition that comes round every year; a keeper of days on the council makes each kept day a small occasion.
The colony is known for the work this colonist loves. It holds as long as the work goes on; the Our ways page shows how close the colony is to each name, and where it stands.
A vendetta ended without more blood: laid down, or the one who was taken came home. The Bonds page keeps how it ended.
